blocks.text: 1.1.4 Properties of the Fundamental Operations on Complex Numbers

Is sabaq mein hum dekhenge ke jo qawaid (rules) real numbers ke hisaab mein chalte hain, kya woh complex numbers par bhi chalte hain. Achhi khabar yeh hai ke haan, qareeb qareeb sab chalte hain. Pichle sabaq mein aap ne ordered pairs \((a, b)\) ki zubaan seekhi thi; ab isi zubaan mein identity, inverse aur distributive law dekhenge, aur aakhir mein complex numbers ki taqseem (division) ka tareeqa seekhenge.

Kitab kehti hai ke yeh aasani se verify kiya ja sakta hai ke set \(C\) tamam field axioms ko poora karta hai, yani is mein real numbers wali saari properties hain. Kuch baaton ki wazahat ke liye yeh dekhiye:

items: Har complex number \((a, b)\) ka additive inverse \((-a, -b)\) hai, yani \[(a, b) + (-a, -b) = (0, 0)\]
Multiplicative identity \((1, 0)\) hai, yani \[(a, b)(1, 0)\] \[= (a\cdot1 - b\cdot0,\ b\cdot1 + a\cdot0)\] \[= (a, b)\] \[= (1, 0)(a, b)\]

Har non-zero complex number (yani jo \((0, 0)\) ke barabar na ho) ka multiplicative inverse hota hai. \((a, b)\) ka multiplicative inverse \[\left(\dfrac{a}{a^2+b^2},\ \dfrac{-b}{a^2+b^2}\right)\] hai, kyunke \[(a, b)\left(\dfrac{a}{a^2+b^2},\ \dfrac{-b}{a^2+b^2}\right)\] \[= (1, 0),\] jo identity element hai, aur yeh \[\left(\dfrac{a}{a^2+b^2},\ \dfrac{-b}{a^2+b^2}\right)(a, b)\] ke barabar bhi hai.

blocks.text: Ab in paanch baaton ko aasan alfaaz mein samajhte hain. "Identity" woh number hai jo kisi number ke saath operation karne par us number ko badalta nahi. Real numbers mein jama ki identity 0 hai (\(5 + 0 = 5\)) aur zarb ki identity 1 hai (\(5 \times 1 = 5\)). Complex numbers mein yeh kaam \((0, 0)\) yani \(0\) aur \((1, 0)\) yani \(1\) karte hain. Point (iii) mein rule (iii) lagaa kar dikhaya gaya hai ke \((a, b)(1, 0)\) wapas \((a, b)\) hi deta hai.

"Inverse" woh number hai jo operation ke baad identity par wapas le aaye. Jama ka inverse "ulta number" hai: \((a, b)\) mein \((-a, -b)\) jama karein to \((0, 0)\) milta hai, bilkul \(5 + (-5) = 0\) ki tarah. Zarb ka inverse "ulta hissa" hai: real numbers mein \(5\) ka inverse \(\frac{1}{5}\) hai. Complex number ka multiplicative inverse thora lamba dikhta hai, lekin neeche hum dekhenge ke yeh bhi \(\frac{1}{a+ib}\) hi hai. Point (v) distributive law hai: bracket ke bahar wala number andar ke har number ko zarb deta hai.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.text: Complex numbers ka set \(C\) order axioms ko poora nahi karta. Asal mein yeh kehna be-maani hai ke ek complex number doosre se bara ya chhota hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
"Field axioms" ka matlab woh jaane pehchane qawaid hain jin se hum real numbers ka hisaab karte hain: jama aur zarb closed hain (jawab bhi isi set mein rehta hai), commutative hain (tarteeb badalne se jawab nahi badalta), associative hain (grouping badalne se jawab nahi badalta); identities \((0,0)\) aur \((1,0)\) mojood hain; har number ka additive inverse aur har non-zero number ka multiplicative inverse mojood hai; aur zarb jama par distribute hoti hai (point (v)). Nateeja: complex numbers ke saath aap bilkul real numbers ki tarah hisaab kar sakte hain.
Complex numbers ko chhota bara kyun nahi keh sakte? Maan lijiye \(i > 0\). Dono taraf positive number \(i\) se zarb dein to \(i \cdot i > 0\), yani \(-1 > 0\), jo ghalat hai. Ab maan lijiye \(i < 0\); to \(-i > 0\), aur \((-i)(-i) > 0\), yani phir \(-1 > 0\), phir ghalat. Aur \(i \ne 0\). Is liye order axioms ke mutabiq koi tarteeb mumkin nahi. (Yeh wazahat hamari hai, kitab mein chhapi nahi.)
Ek misaal se samjhiye: shehar ke naqshe par do jagahon ke baare mein yeh poochhna ke "kaun si bari hai" be-maani hai; haan, yeh poochh sakte hain ke kaun si markaz se zyada door hai. Complex numbers mein bhi sirf un ka faasla (modulus, 1.1.5) compare hota hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Inverse ka formula kahan se aaya? \((a, b)\) ko \(a + ib\) likhiye aur \(\frac{1}{a+ib}\) ke upar neeche conjugate se zarb dijiye:
\[\dfrac{1}{a + ib} = \dfrac{a - ib}{(a + ib)(a - ib)}\]
\[= \dfrac{a - ib}{a^2 + b^2}\]
Yeh wahi pair \(\left(\frac{a}{a^2+b^2}, \frac{-b}{a^2+b^2}\right)\) hai. Yahan \((a, b) \ne (0, 0)\) zaroori hai taake \(a^2 + b^2 \ne 0\) ho; zero se taqseem kisi bhi number system mein mumkin nahi.
Hamari taraf se misaal: \((3, 4)\) ka inverse \(\left(\frac{3}{25}, \frac{-4}{25}\right)\) hai, kyunke \(3^2 + 4^2 = 25\). Formula yaad rakhne ka tareeqa: "conjugate upar, modulus ka square neeche".

Ab kitab ki doosri misaal: do complex numbers ki taqseem. Sab se pehle yeh samajhte hain ke humein find kya karna hai: \(z_1\) ko \(z_2\) se taqseem karna hai. Mushkil yeh hai ke neeche (denominator mein) \(i\) hai, aur \(i\) wale number se seedha taqseem nahi kar sakte. Is liye hum woh chaal chalenge jo pichle sabaq mein dekhi thi: conjugate se zarb, taake neeche real number aa jaye.

blocks.title: Example 2
steps:
Diya gaya (Given): \(z_1 = (4, 2)\), \(z_2 = (3, -1)\).
Maloom karna hai (To find): \(\frac{z_1}{z_2}\).
Tareeqa (Method): pehle pairs ko \(a + ib\) ki shakal mein likhenge, kyunke is shakal mein algebra karna asaan hai. Phir numerator (upar) aur denominator (neeche) dono ko denominator ke conjugate se zarb denge, taake neeche se \(i\) khatam ho jaye aur jawab \(x + iy\) ki shakal mein aa jaye.

Step 1: \(a + ib\) ki shakal mein likhein
\[\dfrac{z_1}{z_2} = \dfrac{(4, 2)}{(3, -1)}\]
\[= \dfrac{4 + 2i}{3 - i}\]
Kyun: pair \((a, b)\) ka matlab \(a + ib\) hai. To \((4, 2) = 4 + 2i\) aur \((3, -1) = 3 + (-1)i = 3 - i\).

Step 2: upar neeche conjugate \(3 + i\) se zarb dein
\[\dfrac{4 + 2i}{3 - i} \times \dfrac{3 + i}{3 + i}\]
Kyun: \(3 - i\) ka conjugate \(3 + i\) hai (sirf imaginary part ka sign badla). \(\frac{3+i}{3+i} = 1\), aur kisi cheez ko 1 se zarb dene se us ki value nahi badalti; sirf shakal badalti hai. Faida yeh ke \((3-i)(3+i)\) mein koi \(i\) nahi bachta, to denominator real ho jata hai.
Dhyan dein: bohat se students yahan numerator ke conjugate se zarb de dete hain. Hamesha denominator (neeche wale) ka conjugate lijiye.

Step 3: numerator
\[(4)(3) + (4)(i) + (2i)(3) + (2i)(i)\]
\[= 12 + 4i + 6i + 2i^2\]
\[= 12 + 10i - 2\]
\[= 10 + 10i\]
Kyun: pehle bracket ka har term doosre bracket ke har term se zarb hota hai, is liye chaar terms bane. Phir \(4i + 6i = 10i\) (like terms). Aakhir mein \(i^2 = -1\) lagaya, to \(2i^2 = 2(-1) = -2\), aur \(12 - 2 = 10\).

Step 4: denominator
\[(3 - i)(3 + i) = (3)^2 - (i)^2\]
\[= 9 - (-1)\]
\[= 10\]
Kyun: yeh identity \((a - b)(a + b) = a^2 - b^2\) hai, jahan \(a = 3\) aur \(b = i\). Phir \(i^2 = -1\), aur \(9 - (-1) = 9 + 1 = 10\).
Dhyan dein: yahan \(9 - 1 = 8\) likhna sab se aam ghalti hai. Minus ka minus plus hota hai.

Step 5: taqseem karein
\[\dfrac{z_1}{z_2} = \dfrac{10 + 10i}{10}\]
\[= 1 + i\]
Kyun: ab neeche real number 10 hai, to real part \(10\) aur imaginary part \(10\) dono ko alag alag 10 se taqseem kar sakte hain: \(\frac{10}{10} + \frac{10}{10}i = 1 + i\).

Tasdeeq (Check):
Agar \(\frac{z_1}{z_2} = 1 + i\) hai to \((1 + i) \times z_2\) ko \(z_1\) dena chahiye. Check karte hain:
\[(1 + i)(3 - i) = 3 - i + 3i - i^2\]
\[= 3 + 1 + 2i\]
\[= 4 + 2i\]
Yeh \(z_1 = (4, 2)\) hi hai, is liye jawab sahi hai.

blocks.title: Exam tip
blocks.text: Complex numbers ki taqseem mein hamesha numerator aur denominator dono ko denominator ke conjugate se zarb dijiye. Denominator \(c^2 + d^2\) ban jata hai, jo real number hai, aur jawab \(x + iy\) ki shakal mein likha ja sakta hai. Aakhri jawab hamesha \(x + iy\) ki shakal mein likhiye; neeche \(i\) chhor dena poora jawab nahi maana jata.

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: \(\frac{1}{i}\) kitna hoga? Upar neeche \(i\) ke conjugate \(-i\) se zarb dijiye: \(\frac{-i}{-i^2} = \frac{-i}{1} = -i\). Yani \(\frac{1}{i} = -i\). Check: \(i \times (-i) = -i^2 = 1\).

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(C\) tamam field axioms poore karta hai; complex numbers ke saath real numbers ki tarah hisaab hota hai.
2. Additive identity \((0, 0)\); \((a, b)\) ka additive inverse \((-a, -b)\).
3. Multiplicative identity \((1, 0)\); \((a, b) \ne (0,0)\) ka inverse \(\left(\frac{a}{a^2+b^2}, \frac{-b}{a^2+b^2}\right)\).
4. \(C\) ordered nahi: complex numbers ke liye \(z_1 > z_2\) ka koi matlab nahi.
5. Taqseem: upar neeche denominator ke conjugate se zarb.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
\(a + ib\) ka inverse \(\frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{ib}\) likh dena. Ghalat! Conjugate wala tareeqa istemaal kijiye.
Inverse mein minus ka sign bhool jana: doosra component \(\frac{-b}{a^2+b^2}\) hai.
\((3-i)(3+i) = 9 - 1 = 8\) likhna. \(i^2 = -1\) hai, is liye jawab \(9 - (-1) = 10\) hai.
Complex numbers ko compare karna, jaise "\(3 + 2i > 1 + i\)". Sirf un ke modulus (1.1.5), jo real numbers hain, compare ho sakte hain.
